meta.title: Income that changes. A plan that stays.
meta.subtitle: A small money habit for daily, weekly and project earners.

coreRule.label: THE ARTHSETU RULE
coreRule.title: Protect tomorrow before upgrading today.
coreRule.body: Do not plan life around your best earning period. First protect money needed to keep earning, then essential household costs, then a buffer, and only then increase lifestyle spending.
coreRule.short: Work first. Home next. Buffer after. Lifestyle last.

welcome.heading: Your income may change. Your plan can stay steady.
welcome.body: Some days are busy. Some weeks are quiet. Some invoices arrive late. This guide helps you decide what to do each time money comes in.

journey.title: TEACH
journey.body: Learn one idea through a familiar Indian work story.

journey.title: PRACTICE
journey.body: Move sample rupees into clear boxes.

journey.title: SELF-PLAN
journey.body: Write a plan you can repeat on your own.

welcome.trust: No login. No bank details. Your plan stays on this device.
welcome.imageCaption: The people who earn every day keep the country moving.

tierPrompt.heading: How does your money arrive?
tierPrompt.body: Choose the pattern that feels closest. You can change it later.

cards.title: Daily / cash
cards.subtitle: Money comes in day by day
cards.audience: Sweepers, vegetable sellers, labourers, auto drivers and other daily earners.
cards.oneLine: Protect today’s earning power for tomorrow.

cards.title: Weekly / gig / shop
cards.subtitle: Payouts or sales come through the week
cards.audience: Delivery partners, ride-hailing drivers, kirana shops and technicians.
cards.oneLine: Business first, steady home draw, then buffer.

cards.title: Invoice / project
cards.subtitle: Money arrives after work or milestones
cards.audience: Freelancers, designers, developers, consultants and independent makers.
cards.oneLine: Every payment needs a job before it is spent.

floor.heading: What must be paid so life and work can continue?
floor.body: Add the minimum for one month. Essentials only. Leave out shopping, eating out and upgrades.

fields.label: Housing / rent
fields.hint: Rent or the minimum home cost

fields.label: School + essential health
fields.hint: School basics, regular medicines, essential care

fields.label: Work cost
fields.hint: Stock, petrol, tools, travel or platform costs

floor.lowMonth: Money received in a weak month (rough estimate)
floor.lowMonthHint: Use a slow month, not your best month. Leave blank if unsure.
floor.example: Illustration only: if home basics are ₹12,000 and work needs ₹3,000, the Floor Number is ₹15,000 for the month.
floor.privacy: Use rounded estimates. Do not enter account numbers, PINs, OTPs, PAN or Aadhaar.

reality.heading: A low month is information, not failure.
reality.belowTitle: This month is below the floor.
reality.belowBody: First goal is not investing. Protect the ability to earn, reduce avoidable leakage, check which support schemes you may qualify for, and build even a tiny cushion when possible. Do not borrow just to keep a lifestyle promise.
reality.nearTitle: The floor may be covered, but keep the order.
reality.nearBody: Protect work money first. Cover essential household costs next. Then build a buffer for slow days and delayed payments. A better month does not make every month a better month.
reality.unknownBody: You can continue without an income estimate. Use the Floor Number as your minimum monthly requirement and compare it with real income as it arrives.
reality.rule: This is not a judgement about how hard you work. It is a tool to make the next decision clearer.

lesson.heading: Learn one small habit at a time.
lesson.body: Read the story, look at the example, then try the tiny action. Use the speaker button to hear the card.
lesson.quizTitle: A quick check — no marks, no shame
lesson.quizHint: Choose what you would actually do. You will see why.
lesson.correct: That is the safer next step.
lesson.tryAgain: Not quite. Have another look at the idea.

practice.heading: Move the money before you spend it.
practice.body: Enter an amount that came in. Choose a box, then drag a coin or tap it. You can also type an amount into each box. These are practice amounts, not rules.
practice.moneyIn: Money received today / this week / this payment
practice.coinHint: Drag a coin to a box, or select a box and tap a coin.
practice.over: The boxes add up to more than the money received. Reduce one amount.
practice.under: Some money is still unassigned. Decide what job it needs before spending it.
practice.balanced: You have placed the full amount. Check the order once more.

boxHints.work: Stock, fuel, tools, travel for tomorrow
boxHints.home: Rent, ration, fees and fixed bills
boxHints.buffer: A reserve for a slow week or late payment
boxHints.tax: A reserve based on your tax estimate

plan.heading: My plan, in my own words.
plan.body: This is a simple reminder, not a strict budget. Change it when your work or household costs change.

fields.label: Money I must protect for work
My first buffer target
fields.placeholder: Start with 1 day, then 1 week, then 1 month

plan.sevenBody: Tick the four habits you will practise this week. Then tick each day you did your small money check. The badge is for repeating a habit, not for saving a big amount.
pledges: Separate work money before household spending.
Write down my minimum essential household cost.
Save part of a good earning day or week for a weak one.
Do not treat peak income as permanent income.
plan.save: Save my plan on this device
plan.saved: Your plan is saved on this device. On a shared phone, another person who opens this app may see it.
plan.cleared: Saved plan cleared from this browser.
plan.privacy: Do not write passwords, OTPs, PINs, bank account numbers, PAN or Aadhaar in this plan.

questions.heading: When money comes in, pause and ask these five questions — in this order.
questions.body: This order protects your ability to earn and your household before lifestyle spending.

items.hint: Protect stock, fuel, transport, tools and work costs.
items.hiLabel: क्या मैं कल भी कमा पाऊँगा?

items.hint: Rent, ration, utilities, school and essential health.
items.hiLabel: क्या जरूरी घर के खर्च पूरे हैं?

items.hint: Save something for a weak day, week or delayed invoice.
items.hiLabel: क्या धीमे समय के लिए बचत बढ़ रही है?

items.q: Do I owe tax or business costs?
items.hint: Keep the money needed for business and any tax due.
items.hiLabel: क्या टैक्स या काम का खर्च बाकी है?

items.q: Only now: can I spend or invest more?
items.hint: Use only what remains after stability is protected.
items.hiLabel: अब क्या मैं अतिरिक्त खर्च या निवेश कर सकता हूँ?

questions.close: The order matters more than the exact split. Your split depends on income, household needs, debt, taxes, eligibility and local costs.

extras.eyebrow: SMALL TOPICS · ABOUT FIVE MINUTES EACH
extras.heading: Useful lessons for real work and real life.
extras.body: Pick one topic. Learn it in a few minutes, then try one small action.

modules.title: Good debt and costly debt
modules.subtitle: Know the full rupee cost before borrowing.

cards.title: Ask what the loan helps you do
cards.story: A loan may help when it protects urgent needs or supports work that can repay it.
cards.idea: A useful loan has a clear purpose and a repayment plan that still works in a weak month.
cards.example: Illustration only: a sewing machine repair helps a tailor keep earning. The instalment must still fit after work costs and essential home costs.
cards.action: Write the purpose and the source of repayment before signing.

cards.title: Look at the total rupees to repay
cards.story: Do not compare only the amount received or the monthly payment.
cards.idea: Ask for the amount you receive, every fee, each due date and the total you must return.
cards.example: Borrow ₹1,000 and repay ₹1,300. The extra cost is ₹300. This is an example only.
cards.action: Ask the lender to write the full repayment amount on paper.

cards.title: Pause before a costly app or lender
cards.story: Pressure, access to contacts/photos, threats and unclear lender details are warning signs.
cards.idea: Use a regulated lender and read the written terms. Do not hand over OTPs or phone access.
cards.example: A neighbour says “₹2,000 now, pay later” but will not show the lender name or full amount. Pause.
cards.action: Do not install an unknown loan app. Verify the lender first.

quiz.question: You receive ₹1,000 and must repay ₹1,300. How much extra is that?
quiz.explain: The extra cost is ₹300. Always compare total rupees to repay.

quiz.question: A lender will not show the full repayment amount. What should you do?
options: Pause and ask for written terms
quiz.explain: Written terms help you see the real cost and due dates.

quiz.question: A loan is safer when…
options: There is a clear purpose and realistic repayment plan
The app asks for contact access
quiz.explain: Purpose and repayment matter more than a tempting promise.

modules.title: Build a buffer in small steps
modules.subtitle: One day. One week. One month.

cards.title: Start with one day
cards.story: A large target can feel impossible. Start with a small amount that protects one day.
cards.idea: The Floor Number is the minimum monthly home-and-work amount. Divide it roughly by 30 for one day.
cards.example: Illustration only: a ₹15,000 monthly Floor Number is about ₹500 per day. The daily figure is a planning shortcut, not a bill.
cards.action: Choose one safe place to keep a one-day cushion.

cards.title: Grow it to one week
cards.story: Add a little during stronger days or weeks.
cards.idea: A one-week target can be estimated as one quarter of the monthly Floor Number.
cards.example: Illustration only: if the floor is ₹15,000, one week is roughly ₹3,750 using the simple one-quarter method.
cards.action: Write your one-week target and review it weekly.

cards.title: Then work toward one month
cards.story: A full month gives more room when work stops or money arrives late.
cards.idea: Keep a buffer separate from daily spending and work cash. Choose a safe, accessible place that fits your situation.
cards.example: A designer waiting for an invoice may use the buffer for rent and food while the client payment is delayed.
cards.action: Do not put emergency money into something whose value can fall or cannot be accessed quickly.

quiz.question: What is a helpful first buffer target?
options: One day of the Floor Number
quiz.explain: Start with one day, then build toward one week and one month.

quiz.question: When should you use the buffer?
options: For a real low-income period or delayed payment
quiz.explain: A buffer protects essentials during a weak period.

quiz.question: Is one universal buffer amount right for everyone?
options: No, it depends on costs and income pattern
quiz.explain: The amount depends on the household and work costs.

modules.title: Digital safety for everyday payments
modules.subtitle: UPI, OTPs and fake loan apps.

cards.title: A PIN is for sending money
cards.story: You do not enter a UPI PIN just to receive money.
cards.idea: A collect request asks you to approve a payment. Read the screen carefully before entering a PIN.
cards.example: A buyer says “I sent a collect request; enter your PIN to receive ₹500.” Stop. A PIN can approve money leaving your account.
cards.action: Never share your UPI PIN or OTP. Do not enter the PIN to receive money.

cards.title: Do not hand over your phone
cards.story: Fraudsters may ask you to install an app, share your screen or read out an OTP.
cards.idea: A bank or government worker should not need your PIN or OTP. Call your bank using the number on its official website or card.
cards.example: A caller says your account will close unless you install a screen-sharing app. End the call and contact your bank independently.
cards.action: Keep screen sharing and unknown app installs off during financial calls.

cards.title: Act quickly after fraud
cards.story: Fast reporting may help banks and authorities trace or stop a transaction.
cards.idea: Call 1930 and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Also contact your bank immediately. Use official channels only.
cards.example: If ₹2,000 leaves your account unexpectedly, report it at once. Keep the transaction reference.
cards.action: Save 1930 in your phone and teach one trusted person how to report.

quiz.question: Do you enter a UPI PIN to receive money?
options: Only if the caller says so
quiz.explain: A UPI PIN authorises a payment from your account.

quiz.question: Someone asks for your OTP to stop a bank account from closing. What do you do?
options: End the call and contact the bank yourself
quiz.explain: Never share OTPs. Contact the bank through a trusted official number.

quiz.question: What is the national cyber financial fraud helpline?
quiz.explain: Call 1930 quickly and report through the official cybercrime portal.

modules.title: Insurance and pension in plain words
modules.subtitle: Protect health, income and later years.

cards.title: Health cover helps with hospital costs
cards.story: Health insurance or an eligible public health scheme may help pay covered hospital bills.
cards.idea: Read who is covered, hospitals, waiting periods, limits and what is not covered.
cards.example: A family discovers that a hospital is not in the cashless network. Checking the list before an emergency can help.
cards.action: Keep policy or scheme details and the claim contact somewhere safe.

cards.title: Accident and life cover do different jobs
cards.story: Accident cover is for listed accident events. Life cover pays according to the policy if the insured person dies.
cards.idea: Check eligibility, exclusions, renewal date, nominee and claim steps. Do not assume every event is covered.
cards.example: A delivery partner wants to know whether a policy covers an accident while working. They must read the exact terms.
cards.action: Ask the insurer or bank to explain exclusions in simple words.

cards.title: Pension needs regular care
cards.story: Some public pension schemes require contributions and have entry conditions.
cards.idea: Check age, income, existing EPF/ESIC/NPS membership, contribution amount and exit rules before joining.
cards.example: PM-SYM is a voluntary contributory scheme for eligible unorganised workers. The contribution depends on joining age and rules.
cards.action: Do not join a scheme until you know the monthly debit and whether you qualify.

quiz.question: What should you check before choosing health cover?
options: Hospitals, exclusions, waiting period and limits
quiz.explain: The cover details matter when you make a claim.

quiz.question: Are accident cover and life cover the same?
quiz.explain: Read the exact event covered by each policy.

quiz.question: A contributory pension scheme means…
options: You may need to pay regularly under its rules
You can stop without checking exit rules
quiz.explain: Understand the amount and conditions before you enrol.

cards.title: Keep a simple work record
cards.story: Write down each invoice, date sent, payment date and amount received.
cards.idea: Record business costs and any tax already deducted. Keep invoices and receipts together.
cards.example: You send an invoice for ₹40,000 in August but receive it in October. Record both dates.
cards.action: Use a notebook or simple spreadsheet; keep a copy of each invoice.

cards.title: Tax is based on the full picture
cards.story: Tax depends on the type of income, expenses, deductions and current law. There is no safe universal tax percentage for every freelancer.
cards.idea: Estimate annual tax with a qualified tax professional or official tax tools. Check whether advance tax applies.
cards.example: A designer receives ₹50,000 but also has work costs and other income. The amount to keep for tax needs a proper calculation, not a guess.
cards.action: Keep a tax reserve only after checking your likely tax with a professional.

cards.title: Know when advance tax may apply
cards.story: The Income Tax Department explains that advance tax can apply when the estimated tax payable after relevant credits reaches the official threshold.
cards.idea: For current tax year rules, use incometax.gov.in or ask a qualified tax professional. The rules changed with the Income-tax Act, 2025.
cards.example: A freelancer has irregular invoices but tax dates still arrive on the calendar. Planning for dates avoids a surprise.
cards.action: Mark official tax dates only after checking the current year guidance.

quiz.question: What should you record for each invoice?
options: Invoice date, amount, payment date and related costs
quiz.explain: Records make it easier to estimate cash flow and tax.

quiz.question: Is one tax percentage correct for all freelancers?
quiz.explain: Tax depends on the full income picture and current rules.

quiz.question: Where should you check current tax rules?
options: The official Income Tax Department portal or a qualified professional
quiz.explain: Use official and professional sources for tax decisions.

modules.title: Why a peak season is not permanent income
modules.subtitle: Keep your life steady when sales jump.

cards.title: Compare a strong period with a weak one
cards.story: A busy festival week or a large client payment may not repeat next month.
cards.idea: Plan using a weak or normal period, not the highest amount you remember.
cards.example: Ramesh earns ₹600 on a good day and ₹200 on a bad day. The ₹600 day should not set a new daily lifestyle.
cards.action: Write one good-day amount and one weak-day amount.

cards.title: Keep the extra for the lean period
cards.story: After work costs and essential home costs are protected, a strong period can help build the buffer.
cards.idea: Do not treat every rupee left after a good day as free-to-spend money.
cards.example: A shop has a festival week with more sales. The owner first replaces stock, covers home needs and keeps money for the quiet weeks.
cards.action: Before a large purchase, check whether the slow-period buffer is on track.

cards.title: Delay upgrades until your base is steady
cards.story: A bigger phone, vehicle or rent commitment can continue after the peak season ends.
cards.idea: Test a new recurring cost against a weak month and its repayment or maintenance needs.
cards.example: A driver has a strong week and considers a higher vehicle EMI. They first test whether a slow week can still cover it.
cards.action: Wait, calculate the weak-month cost, then decide.

quiz.question: Ramesh earns ₹600 on a good day and ₹200 on a bad day. Which amount should guide fixed spending?
options: A cautious amount that can survive weaker days
quiz.explain: A high day is not permanent. Build the plan around a realistic low period.

quiz.question: What should happen to extra peak-season money?
options: Protect work, home essentials and buffer first
quiz.explain: The order keeps work and home stable through lean periods.

quiz.question: Before taking on a monthly EMI, test it against…
quiz.explain: Recurring costs continue even when income falls.

safety.heading: Government support: check eligibility before you count on it.
safety.body: These schemes do not automatically apply to everyone. Use official sites or a local government help centre to check your own eligibility and the latest rules.
safety.warning: Registration is not the same as receiving cash or a benefit. Some schemes are insurance, pension contributions, loans or work entitlements. Read the terms before signing or paying.

facilitator.heading: A 30-minute session that respects everyone’s work.
facilitator.body: Use sample stories and blank sheets. Do not ask anyone to announce income, debt, Aadhaar, account details or personal hardship. People may pass on any question.

schedule.title: Welcome without judgement
schedule.body: Say: “Income changes for many kinds of work. Today we will learn a simple order, not compare earnings.” Ask people to name different kinds of work, not their own income.

schedule.title: Tell one local work story
schedule.body: Use Ramesh: ₹600 on a good day, ₹200 on a weak day. Ask: “What must he keep so he can work tomorrow?” Introduce the Work → Home → Buffer → Lifestyle order.

schedule.title: Find a Floor Number
schedule.body: Give a blank card with housing, ration/utilities, school/essential health and work costs. Let people use imaginary numbers or keep their sheet private.

schedule.title: Move sample rupees
schedule.body: Use paper tokens. Ask the group to place work costs first, then essential home costs, then buffer, then any extra. Discuss why a strong day is not the same as a stable month.

schedule.title: Practise the five questions
schedule.body: Read each question slowly. Ask participants to point to the icon or repeat the order. Do not pressure anyone to share their own plan.

schedule.title: One private next step
schedule.body: Everyone chooses one habit for the next seven days. Share official support links and explain how to verify eligibility. Thank people for their time.

discussion: What work cost must be protected before tomorrow?
Which household costs cannot be delayed?
What changes between a busy week and a slow week?
Where could a one-day buffer be kept safely?
Which official help source could we check together?
facilitator.care: Facilitator note: never collect or photograph completed plans. Do not promise loan approval, cash benefits or scheme eligibility.

footer.disclaimer: Financial education only. This is not personalised investment, tax, insurance or legal advice. Amounts are examples, not instructions. Check current rules with the official source before acting.
footer.privacy: Your plan is stored only in this browser on this device. Shared phones are not private.

cards.title: Keep tomorrow’s work alive
cards.story: Ramesh sells vegetables. Before he thinks about home spending, he must buy fresh stock and keep money for transport.
cards.idea: Money needed to earn again is not free-to-spend money. Put stock, petrol, tools and travel first.
cards.example: Illustration only: Ramesh earns ₹600 on a good day and ₹200 on a weak day. The amount for tomorrow’s stock must be protected before he spends.
cards.action: Name the one cost that lets you work tomorrow.

cards.title: Make three physical boxes
cards.story: Ramesh keeps three envelopes at home: Work First, Home Fixed and Today.
cards.idea: Use three boxes or envelopes. Label them clearly. Put work money in the first, a daily share for fixed home costs in the second, and daily needs in the third.
cards.example: Illustration only: the labels matter more than a fixed split. Ramesh decides the amounts after checking stock cost and the home floor.
cards.action: Make three paper labels today.

cards.title: Fix the home amount carefully
cards.story: Rent, ration and school costs come every month, even when sales change.
cards.idea: Estimate the minimum monthly home cost. Divide it into a daily amount only as a planning aid. If income is too low, do not pretend the full amount is available.
cards.example: Illustration only: a ₹6,000 fixed home amount across 30 days is about ₹200 a day. Some days may not be able to contribute this much.
cards.action: Write the monthly home amount and review it after one week.

cards.title: Today’s money is for today’s needs
cards.story: After work money and the fixed home share, Ramesh can see what is left for food and daily needs.
cards.idea: Use the Today box for current food and daily needs. If there is not enough, check priorities and support options; do not hide the gap with a costly loan.
cards.example: Illustration only: if ₹100 remains, it is ₹100—not ₹300. Do not spend money that has another job.
cards.action: At day end, count what is left before spending it.

cards.title: Close the day with one note
cards.story: A small note helps Ramesh see whether the same amount is enough every day.
cards.idea: Write money received, work money kept, home amount and what remained. This is a learning record, not a complicated budget.
cards.example: Illustration only: “Sales ₹600; stock and travel ₹220; home envelope ₹150; left ₹230.” Actual amounts change by day.
cards.action: Make one four-line note at the end of work.

quiz.question: What goes into the first box?
quiz.explain: Work money keeps earning possible tomorrow.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of Home Fixed?
options: A daily share for rent, ration and fees
quiz.explain: It helps prepare for costs that come every month.

quiz.question: If today’s income is low, what should you do first?
options: Pretend it was a good day
Protect essential work costs and review urgent needs
quiz.explain: A weak day needs a calm reality check, not a forced spending target.

cards.title: Sales are not your real earning
cards.story: A kirana shop receives money from sales, but some of it must buy stock and pay electricity, delivery and repairs.
cards.idea: First remove the costs of keeping the business open. The remaining amount is closer to the money available for home and buffer.
cards.example: Illustration only: a peak week has ₹12,000 sales and ₹4,500 work costs. ₹7,500 remains before household draw and buffer.
cards.action: Write sales and work costs as two separate lines.

cards.title: Compare a peak week and a slow week
cards.story: A delivery partner may receive higher app payouts during a busy week and much less in a quiet week.
cards.idea: Compare at least one strong week and one slow week. Subtract fuel, maintenance, platform fees and other work costs in both.
cards.example: Illustration only: slow-week payouts ₹7,000 minus ₹3,800 costs leaves ₹3,200. Do not treat the peak amount as a permanent salary.
cards.action: Keep one note for a strong week and one for a slow week.

cards.title: Give the household a steady weekly draw
cards.story: The shop or app account should not become the family’s daily spending wallet.
cards.idea: Choose a fixed weekly household amount that can still work in a weak period. Transfer it from business money after essential business costs.
cards.example: Illustration only: a shop owner chooses a small weekly draw after checking slow-week earnings. The amount is personal to that shop, not a rule for all shops.
cards.action: Choose a review day for the weekly household transfer.

cards.title: Keep the buffer for the quiet season
cards.story: Festival weeks, rain, repairs or low demand can reduce sales.
cards.idea: After business costs and the planned home draw, keep part of stronger weeks for the next slow week.
cards.example: Illustration only: if a peak week leaves more after costs than the household draw, the extra can help cover a weaker week.
cards.action: Name one season when your work usually slows.

cards.title: Separate business and personal money
cards.story: When QR payouts, app income and household payments mix together, it is hard to know what the business really earned.
cards.idea: Use separate accounts, envelopes or a notebook column for business and personal money. Reconcile sales and costs regularly.
cards.example: Illustration only: ₹2,000 in QR sales is not ₹2,000 free to spend if stock still needs to be replaced.
cards.action: At closing, write total sales, work costs and personal draw.

quiz.question: A shop has ₹12,000 sales and ₹4,500 costs. What remains before the home draw and buffer?
quiz.explain: ₹12,000 − ₹4,500 = ₹7,500. It is not all personal spending money.

quiz.question: Why compare a strong week with a slow week?
options: To prove the business is always growing
quiz.explain: A slow-week check makes the household amount more realistic.

quiz.question: Where should extra money from a strong week go first?
options: A slow-season buffer after work costs and home draw
quiz.explain: Peak income can help carry the business and household through quiet weeks.

cards.title: Work done is not payment received
cards.story: A designer finishes a project in July, but the client pays in September. Rent and software costs continue before the money arrives.
cards.idea: Treat delayed invoices as normal. Keep a list of work delivered, invoice sent, due date and actual payment date.
cards.example: Illustration only: an invoice for ₹40,000 is sent today but arrives after 45 days. It cannot pay today’s rent until it arrives.
cards.action: Write the next invoice due date and follow-up date.

cards.title: Give every payment four jobs
cards.story: When a client pays, the money needs to cover tax, business operations, personal draw and a buffer.
cards.idea: Split the payment into four labelled places. Work out tax with a qualified professional; do not copy a percentage from someone else.
cards.example: Illustration only: a ₹50,000 payment might have ₹8,000 business costs, a ₹7,000 tax placeholder based on an individual estimate, ₹20,000 personal draw and ₹15,000 buffer. These figures are not a recommendation.
cards.action: Make four labels: Tax, Business, Personal, Buffer.

cards.title: Keep a tax and records folder
cards.story: Invoices, business receipts, bank credits and tax deducted at source can matter when working out tax.
cards.idea: Keep dated records of invoices, expenses, payments and tax documents. Check current rules on the Income Tax Department portal.
cards.example: Illustration only: a ₹5,000 software receipt is a record of a work cost. Whether and how it counts for tax depends on the rules and your facts.
cards.action: Put this month’s invoices and receipts in one folder.

cards.title: Pay yourself from a steady base
cards.story: A large project payment can feel like a high salary, but another project may take weeks to arrive.
cards.idea: Choose a personal draw based on a realistic low period, after tax and business needs. Do not make a new monthly commitment from one large invoice.
cards.example: Illustration only: a freelancer receives ₹80,000 for one project. That does not mean ₹80,000 will arrive every month.
cards.action: Write your base personal draw and the date you review it.

cards.title: Invest only after stability is protected
cards.story: Tax, work costs, home essentials and buffer all have a job before surplus becomes available.
cards.idea: Use only genuine surplus after known obligations and a suitable buffer. Take tax and investment advice from qualified professionals.
cards.example: Illustration only: if ₹10,000 remains after all required amounts, the person can review it as surplus. The right next step depends on their situation.
cards.action: Ask: “Is this money truly extra, or does it already have a job?”

quiz.question: A project is finished but the invoice is unpaid. What should your plan show?
options: Invoice date, due date and actual receipt date
quiz.explain: Work completed and cash received are different dates.

quiz.question: What are the four jobs for a project payment?
quiz.explain: The four labels help keep obligations visible.

quiz.question: Should you copy a tax percentage from another freelancer?
options: No, estimate using your own facts and current rules
quiz.explain: Tax depends on your own income and rules. Ask a qualified professional.
